description: Run 35B MoE models in ~2.5 GB of RAM. Weights stream from SSD; a trained router predicts loads a step ahead. Mac, iPhone, Android, Windows supported

summary.one_liner: edge0 is an open-source streaming MoE inference framework that runs large sparse-MoE models (35B and 8B tiers) on consumer hardware by streaming expert weights from SSD and using a trained router to prefetch them.
summary.what_it_does: The framework loads sparse-MoE checkpoints in 4-bit and streams expert weights from storage on demand, so peak memory is bounded by the active expert set rather than the total parameter count. A trained prerouter head predicts expert routing one step ahead so expert loads overlap the forward pass; the README reports up to +59% decode throughput. LoRA adapters (Recover-LoRA) are trained by distillation against the fp16 teacher and kept unmerged, so one read-only base can serve several adapter sets. The Python framework runs on macOS with Apple Silicon via MLX and provides a CLI (demo, serve, chat) and an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint, plus a Python API via AutoEngine. Separate platform engines for macOS (Rust), iOS (Swift + MLX Swift), Android (Kotlin + native engine) and Windows (C++ + Vulkan) are in subdirectories, each with its own README. The README includes OpenCompass benchmarks showing an average loss of 3.9 points (edge0-35b) and 2.8 points (edge0-8b) versus the fp16 base models.
use_cases: run a large mixture-of-experts model on a laptop with limited RAM
serve a local OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint on Apple Silicon
run a quantized LLM on an iPhone or Android device
benchmark streaming expert offload versus fully loaded models
experiment with LoRA adapters on a frozen 4-bit base
research on expert routing prediction and SSD-backed inference
notable: SSD expert offload: expert weights are mmapped and read on demand, so peak MLX memory is ~2.9 GiB for the 35B tier
Trained prerouter predicts expert routing one step ahead to overlap loads with compute
Recover-LoRA adapters stay unmerged; a single read-only base can serve multiple adapter sets
Platform engines for macOS, iOS, Android and Windows are open-sourced in subdirectories
Adapters and checkpoint live in one model directory and load automatically
caveats: The Python framework supports only macOS on Apple Silicon for now; CUDA backend is roadmap only
Checkpoints are large (~23 GB for edge0-35b, ~4.2 GB for edge0-8b) and both LoRA and prerouter adapters are required for the full pipeline

Benchmarks show cold-start prefill and decode speeds that are modest (e.g. 14.9-17.7 tok/s decode for 35b on a Mac mini M4 Pro), and the unified cross-platform framework is not yet released (planned Q4 2026)
